There will be some overlap between measures for prophylaxis and treatment of mucositis, and another systematic review4 of treatment strategies found that there was some evidence that top- ical allopurinol or granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor might improve chemotherapy-induced oral mucositis, but the evidence was weak and unreliable. Given the number of var- iables involved in the development of mucositis it is unlikely that any one prophylactic or treatment regimen will prove suitable for all patients. 1. Knox JJ, et al. Management of tumour lysis syn- drome is based on hydration, correction of metabolic abnormal- ities, and supportive treatment of renal failure.1-3 Aggressive hy- dration with isotonic sodium chloride reduces concentrations of uric acid, phosphate, and potassium, and should be considered in all patients at risk of the syndrome, except those at risk of volume overload.
